beats.text: AI can write code, but it fails at scientific discovery. It treats research like a keyword search, missing the deep intuition that defines breakthrough science.
beats.visual_focus: A massive, chaotic library of papers collapsing into a single, glowing node.

beats.text: Think of a standard agent as a librarian who only knows the Dewey Decimal system, while a scientist knows which hidden paper actually unlocks the problem.
beats.visual_focus: Split screen: A rigid index card system vs. a web of interconnected, glowing research nodes.

beats.text: ScholarCatalyst changes this by using 184 lead authors to annotate citation logic, creating a ground-truth dataset for what actually advances a research project.
beats.visual_focus: A graph of 207 papers connecting via human-labeled edges, forming a dense, expert-validated knowledge map.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook actually caught me because I'm tired of seeing AI 'coding' demos that are just glorified autocomplete. I liked the librarian analogy—it's not condescending, it actually makes sense. However, when you dropped 'Recall@20', I had to pause and think if you meant a specific metric or just a general success rate. It's a bit jargon-heavy for a 30-second short, but at least it's real technical data and not some 'magic AI drawer' nonsense.
